text.p: Britain's biggest chemist Boots Co Plc on Thursday reported an 11 percent sales increase in the first quarter, but disappointment over weaker-than-expected contributions from some of its businesses hit the group's shares.
The firm's core retail chain Boots The Chemist increased comparable store sales by 5.1 percent in the three months to end June 1997, which was even beat some market expectations.

But home improvement chain Do It All did less well with a 2.4 percent increase in sales on a like-for-like basis. Retail analysts said this suggested it was not sharing in the Do It Yourself boom to the same extent as its rivals.

They also expressed disappointment at the performance from Boots' over-the-counter healthcare business Boots Healthcare International, where sales, excluding the impact of currencies and acquisitions fell short of predictions.

BHI's comparable sales were up 5.9 percent, against some forecasts for a rise of as much as 15 percent. Retail analysts were disappointed by sharp declines in non-core products, despite very strong growth from analgesic and cold remedies Nurofen and Stepsils.
Retail analysts said profit-taking had also knocked the shares back after a steep climb. They stood 30 pence lower at 786 pence.
Mark Charnock, analyst at Charterhouse Tilney, said the results from the core chemist chain looked sound but other parts of the group were less promising.

"If Boots the Chemists is doing OK it should be good news for the company as a whole," Charnock said. "But the shares had risen a hell of a long way and sometimes people just wait for an event like this to crystallise some profits."

Another analyst, who asked not to be identified, said despite the share price fall he would not reduce his earnings forecast for the current year, which was for pretax profits of 580 million pounds. His recommendation on the shares, now at a premium to the market, remained "add".
Boots said the poor weather in June had hit UK sales of sun preparations and hay fever remedies but there were good levels of growth elsewhere at Boots the Chemists.

Chief executive Lord Blyth said a statement to the annual meeting, "Looking ahead, market conditions continue to be satisfactory for our businesses. We believe that we have strategies and people in place to continue the delivery of long term growth."
Sales at Boots Opticians were up 24 percent on a like for like basis in the first quarter.

Chairman Sir Michael Angus said competition remained strong in the current year for Boots' business but consumer confidence was still there, "supported in part by the 'feel good factor' generated by windfall bonuses from the financial sector."

Angus told shareholders a lot of the windfall cash seemed to being spent on holidays, and big ticket items such as televisions and cookers. But Boots would benefit as the entire consumer economy became more prosperous.

Official statistics on Wednesday showed retail sales surged 5.4 percent last month, with rocketing sales of household goods suggesting people are spending and not saving cash received from the demutualisation of building societies, such as the Halifax and Alliance and Leicester.
Boots also revealed its board had been looking at the possibility of splitting its shares, which until today were above eight pounds each.
The issue was raised by a shareholder at the company's annual meeting.
Joint group managing director David Thompson said the board had a meeting on Wednesday that considered the issue of a share split.
"It is at least in our minds," he said.
Chief executive Lord Blyth also said the company was considering a share split.
